import pandas as pd
import io
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Dataset as a string
data = """date,time,product,size,price,quantity,payment_method,customer_age_group,is_takeaway,total
2024-01-01,00:00,Cappuccino,Large,4.18,2,Credit Card,55+,1,8.36
2024-01-01,02:00,Cappuccino,Medium,4.01,3,Credit Card,35-44,1,12.03
2024-01-01,04:00,Tea,Small,5.22,1,Credit Card,18-24,1,5.22
2024-01-01,06:00,Latte,Large,6.37,2,Credit Card,45-54,1,12.74
2024-01-01,08:00,Americano,Medium,7.07,3,Cash,45-54,1,21.21
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Convert 'date' and 'time' to datetime objects if needed for other analyses
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])

# Aggregate total sales by product and customer age group
# This will help understand which products are popular among which age groups
agg_df = df.groupby(['product', 'customer_age_group'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set a professional style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.barplot(
    data=agg_df,
    x='product',
    y='total',
    hue='customer_age_group',
    palette='viridis',
    errorbar=None # No error bars needed for aggregated sums
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Customer Age Group', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)
plt.legend(title='Customer Age Group', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout() # Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png')
